gallery.title: File:Tournai marble font in Winchester Cathedral.jpg
gallery.source: Tournai marble font in Winchester Cathedral
gallery.description: Stone font, brought from Tournai in Belgium to Winchester Cathedral in 12th century. The four sides of the font are decorated with sculpted scenes from the legendary life of St Nicholas. This panel includes a ship, which is the earliest depiction of a ship with a fixed stern rudder and high prow.  The font is carved from carboniferous limestone.

gallery.title: File:Winchestercathedralbluering.jpg
gallery.description: Gold ring from Winchester Cathedral in Winchester, England. Exhibit tag reads: "Ring, Late 12th or early 13th century. Gold set with a sapphire or an aquamarine. 103. This ring was found c. 1813 in a coffin in the nave of Winchester Cathedral. the coffin also contained a crozier. If the burial was that of a bishop the possibilities are Richard Toclyve d. 1189, Godfrey de Lucy d. 1204 but who was buried in the retroquire, or Peter des Roches, d. 1238."
categories: Bishops of the Diocese of Winchester
Taken with Canon EOS-1D Mark III

gallery.title: File:Winchestercathedralshaftesburybowl.jpg
gallery.description: The Shaftesbury Bowl from Winchester Cathedral in Winchester, England. Exhibit tag reads: "The Shaftesbury Bowl, late 10th century. Glass. 98. This glass jar was found in front of the High Altar at Shaftesbury Abbey in 1862 or 1904, and may have contained the heart of King Canute who died at Shaftesbury in c. 1035 but was buried in Winchester. It is the only complete piece of late Saxon glass in England."
categories: Taken with Canon EOS-1D Mark III
